ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Bermuda: Companies Act 1981, Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Regulations 2015, Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Amendment Regulations 2019, and the Bermuda Financial Intelligence Agency directives. Gibraltar: Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (POCA), Sanctions Act 2019, Companies Act 2014, Register of Beneficial Owners Act 2017, and AML/CFT Rules and Guidance issued by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC). UK Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018 and OFSI financial sanctions framework apply to Gibraltar as a British Overseas Territory.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Bermuda Exempted Company
Registered Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association
Register of Beneficial Owners and UBO/Significant Control Worksheet
Directors' and Officers' Appointments and Consent Forms
Gibraltar external company registration statement and power of attorney

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, franchise counterparties, and beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, UK OFSI Consolidated List, Gibraltar administered sanctions list, Bermuda regulated sanctions, and domestic/regional PEP databases. Positive PEP or sanctions matches require enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and, where necessary, GFSC or Bermuda FIA reporting before incorporation or franchise licensing proceeds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Registrar of Companies e-Services portal and Gibraltar Companies House e-Registry (foreign company registration module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be submitted in English using Latin-script alphabetical characters only. Non-Latin script names are not registrable. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name in either Bermuda or Gibraltar. Franchise brands and trademarks may be protected in other languages but cannot form the official registered legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, file a written request for reconsideration with the Bermuda Registrar of Companies and, if applicable, the Gibraltar Companies Registry within 14 business days of the rejection notice; include the re-judgment request, revised name, and commercial justification. If the rejection is sustained, lodge a formal administrative appeal with the Bermuda Supreme Court or Gibraltar Supreme Court, as applicable, within 42 days of the second refusal. Name clearance must be completed before incorporation filing; only the official reserved name may be relied upon in the incorporation certificate.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual-only office is not permissible for the Bermuda Exempted Company statutory registered office: a licensed Bermuda corporate service provider must maintain a physical registered office and local registered agent. For Gibraltar external company registration, a physical service address managed by a licensed corporate services provider is acceptable; a purely virtual mailbox with no local personnel or document-receiving capacity will be rejected. The franchise-licensing and syrup supply-chain model has no point-of-sale in Gibraltar, so a registered-office arrangement must nevertheless ensure real administrative substance for AML/CFT and process service.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annual risk. Unannounced on-site inspections are risk-based and primarily occur at the licensed corporate service provider's premises, rather than at any franchise customer location, because the entity's activity is standard-low-risk beverage-franchise licensing with no direct food handling in Gibraltar.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2014 (Laws of Gibraltar, Cap. 158), ss. 1-25 (Incorporation), ss. 26-38 (Share Capital and Certificates); Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar), ss. 5-6 (Tax Residence and Exempt-Status Election); Companies (Fees) Regulations 2015
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar, Registry General Division, H.M. Government of Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association executed as a Deed, filed together with Form N-02 'Application for Incorporation' and statutory consents
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; standard issued capital is GBP 1.00 per subscriber share. The Exempted-Company template permits 100% non-resident ownership, no exchange control, and no public filing of beneficial ownership until issued capital exceeds USD 10,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the subscription specified in the Statement of First Subscribers be accepted and the initial allotment of ordinary shares be issued at par to the founding subscribers; (2) that the registered office of the Company be established at [Registered Office Address], Gibraltar, and the Directors waive formal notice thereof; (3) that [Name] be and is hereby appointed Director, and [Name] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary, each to serve until the next Annual General Meeting; (4) that the Directors be authorized to open corporate bank accounts, including with an Electronic Money Institution, and to execute the necessary mandates; and (5) that the use of a common seal is dispensed with.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form NC1 'Name Clearance Request' online or by post with two ranked proposed names ending in 'Limited'. Await issuance of the Name Clearance Certificate confirming the name is not identical or confusingly similar to a name already on the Gibraltar register.
required_dossiers: Copy of director's and shareholder's passport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as identical or confusingly similar, refile with an alternative name within 10 working days; appeal the Registrar's decision by statutory declaration under Companies Act 2014 s.20.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Memorandum and Articles and Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form N-02, the registered office consent, and signed consents of the initial director and company secretary. Pay the statutory incorporation fee and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Bermuda-exempted-company style clauses)
Consent to Act as Company Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query (e.g., unlawful objects or missing consents), cure by filing an amended schedule or corrected form within 14 days; voluntary amendment prior to certificate issuance incurs no penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the Certificate of Incorporation, open the statutory registers (members, directors, secretaries, charges, and PSC register), and issue share certificates to the founding subscribers. File the return of allotment within 10 days of allotment.
required_dossiers: Share Register and PSC Register templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request rectification of register entries via the Registrar's Correction Notice procedure; late filing of the return of allotment is cured by filing within 14 days with a late-filing declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Income Tax Office, H.M. Government of Gibraltar (Commissioner of Income Tax)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IT-Exempt together with the board resolution confirming that central management and control is exercised outside Gibraltar, thereby electing non-resident tax status under Income Tax Act 2010 ss. 5-6. Obtain the written non-resident certificate from the Commissioner.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution on non-resident status
Evidence of offshore central management (board minutes from Bermuda or holding company)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commissioner assesses the company as Gibraltar-resident, refile with a revised factual matrix within 30 days or appeal to the Income Tax Tribunal under Income Tax Act 2010 s. 116.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Statutory Company Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass written resolutions to adopt the registered office, allot subscriber shares, approve the corporate bank account opening with an Electronic Money Institution, and appoint initial officers. Update the statutory registers and file any changes with Companies House within 14 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Apply for a late-filing grace period; pay any applicable late filing penalty if statutory register updates are not completed within the mandated window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Environmental Health Department, Gibraltar Health Authority (licensing board for food premises and beverage manufacturing)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Operator Approval and Operating License (Food Safety Act 2014; Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 as applied in Gibraltar)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change (DEHCC), Environmental Agency Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category A-2 Registration (environmental screening required for beverage manufacturing footprint up to 2,000 m²; full EIA Report only if bottling/canning capacity exceeds 10,000 m³ per year or food waste disposal exceeds 1 tonne per day)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to Gibraltar foul sewer must comply with pH 6.0-9.0, BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L, and total suspended solids not exceeding 60 mg/L; no volatile organic compound emissions above EU Directive 2008/50/EC thresholds; HACCP plan required for syrup production; food waste must be collected by licensed carriers under the Waste Framework (Gibraltar) Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service certification under the Fire Safety Act 2011 for commercial cooking, ventilation systems and means of escape; Building Control structural load inspection for equipment mezzanines under the Building Act 2014; occupational health clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act (Gibraltar) covering risk assessment, COSHH compliance for cleaning chemicals, and food hygiene certification by the Environmental Health Department.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (Commissioner of Income Tax; e-filing via the Government of Gibraltar portal at https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi); Gibraltar Customs and Excise Department for indirect/customs taxes; Gibraltar Companies Registry (operated within the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission) for external company branch registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File an external company registration with the Gibraltar Companies Registry within one month of establishing a place of business, submitting certified Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation, constitutional documents, director register, and a Gibraltar registered-office address. Step 2: Apply through the Government of Gibraltar portal for a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN) using the non-resident company with permanent establishment profile; the Commissioner of Income Tax issues the TRN and, where staff are engaged, an employer PAYE and Social Security reference simultaneously. Step 3: Register with Gibraltar Customs and Excise for a Customs Operator Code if goods are to be imported or exported. Step 4: File annual income tax returns and audited branch financial statements; the Gibraltar branch is taxed on a territorial basis while the Bermuda parent remains tax-exempt in Bermuda.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: the Bermuda Exempted Company is exempt from Bermuda income tax (except for in-scope multinational groups subject to the Bermuda Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 at 15% for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2025). Its Gibraltar branch is an opaque permanent establishment of an external company chargeable at Gibraltar's standard 12.5% corporate rate solely on Gibraltar-source trading profits, with participation exemption, IP box, and territorial sourcing reliefs available; no pass-through treatment exists at entity level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available because the Bermuda Exempted Company is a per-se corporation under U.S. Treasury Regulation §301.7701-2(b)(8) and is opaque for Gibraltar tax purposes. Gibraltar does, however, permit elections under the Income Tax Act 2010 to apply the participation exemption, the 50% partial exemption for intra-group financing income, and the patent-box regime to qualifying IP. Hybrid mismatch alignment elections under the Gibraltar Income Tax (Hybrid Mismatches) Rules 2017 may also be filed to pre-empt UK anti-hybrid counteraction under Finance Act 2016, Part VI, where the structure would otherwise produce double-deduction or deduction/non-inclusion outcomes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England and HM Treasury hold monetary jurisdiction; the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) supervises licensed banks, the Government of Gibraltar maintains note-issuing authority under the Currency Notes Act, and the Gibraltar pound (GIP) is fixed at par with GBP (1:1) with full interchangeability. No distinct central bank control over FX beyond UK/EU sanctions and AML obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under Gibraltar law and UK monetary policy. There is no exchange-control permission, no restriction on profit remittance, and no residual requirement to seek Bank of England consent. Corporate distributions, royalty remittances, and capital repatriation from a Gibraltar-resident or Bermuda-exempted company are lawful and unrestricted subject to anti-money laundering (JMLSG/GFSC circulars) and the UK Economic Crime (Anti-Money Laundering) Levy reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Gibraltar and the United Kingdom impose no mandatory surrender or conversion ratio for export proceeds. Exporters may retain proceeds in any permitted currency; however, banking reporting obligations under UK/GFSC AML Regulations and EU Sanctions/UNFSF asset-freeze regimes require purpose-of-payment coding and automatic suspicious transaction reporting for cash or wire amounts above EUR 10,000 equivalent.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low. Leading UK/Gibraltar digital EMIs (e.g., Revolut Business, Wise, Mettle) accept onboarding for a Bermuda Exempted Company with a clean registry profile, but restrict high-frequency franchise royalty collections, bulk syrup supplier settlements, and use of funds for persistent B2B trade. Offshore/boutique EMIs are viable only for overflow multi-currency balances and pre-funded 'chest' accounts; the primary treasury rail must be a Tier 1 clearing bank account in Gibraltar or the UK with SWIFT correspondent access.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted for non-resident corporate clients without physical office presence in Gibraltar, provided the ultimate beneficial owner(s) and a senior authorised signatory complete an approved video/telephonic interview. Certain dedicated private banks (Lombard Odier, Turicum) may impose discretionary in-person Board attendance for first meeting or for relationships above GBP 5 million turnover. Bermuda Exempted Company registry documents must be legalised or apostilled and sent by courier; no in-person visit is strictly mandated by statute.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda Exempted Company structure utilises nominee shareholders and a corporate service provider as registered agent, creating a veil over ultimate beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) certified copy of the Certificate of Exemption and Memorandum of Association from the Bermuda Registrar of Companies; (ii) completed Bermuda Beneficial Ownership (BO) Register return with encrypted UBO IDs; (iii) up-to-date register of directors and members; (iv) each UBO's notarised passport and proof of address (<3 months); (v) signed declaration of non-nominee status or nominee trust deed with full underlying disclosure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Franchise royalty revenue is composed of many small inbound SWIFT payments from sub-franchisees across tea shops, triggering a mixed pattern of 'cash-intensive retail' financial flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Aggregated royalty model spreadsheet; signed master franchise agreements and minimum annual royalty schedules; monthly POS/MIS reports from each sub-franchisee; breakdown of royalties vs. syrup sales to reconcile against predicted cash-flow curves; external audit report by an ICAEW/CPA firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Syrup and CAPEX supply-chain payments to Asian/Chinese ingredient suppliers attract enhanced sanctions and trade-finance screens, particularly for a tax-exempt offshore entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Harmonised System (HS) codes and product allergen/ingredient certificates for ISIC 5610; commercial invoices and B/L/AWB copies; supplier's regulatory licence (food import/export); proof of tobacco-free/sanction-free materials; letter of indemnity from a London freight forwarder.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections from the Bermuda parent/beneficial owners must be wired by MT103/MT202 from a top-tier clearing bank to the Gibraltar operational account, with the beneficiary reference stating 'SHARE CAPITAL – FRANCHISE EXPANSION'. The bank's foreign remittance desk requires a purpose code of 'FOCP' or 'INVE' if the bank applies UK BOP/ITRS classification. The sender must also provide a board resolution resolving to increase paid-in capital and a source-of-funds letter, and the account holding bank should issue a formal 'Certificate of Inward Capital' to be filed with the Bermuda Corporate Registry and Gibraltar tax advisors.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For all franchise royalty distributions to the Bermuda exempted parent and for syrup supply vendors, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 through a UK or Gibraltar clearing direct-clearing correspondent. For large one-off ingredient procurement, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (MT700) with a 30–60 day usance period should be issued; settlement follows SWIFT MT202 vouchers and MT754 advice. Standby LC (MT760) can support sureties on franchise arrangements. Regular disbursements under £50,000 can use sterling or euro instant-clearing rails (FPS/SEPA) if held within UK/EEA bank branch, but tax-relevant transactions must retain MT103 traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forward (vanilla) – available against GIP/GBP, USD, EUR and USD, with 1-week to 12-month tenors from the Gibraltar clearing bank
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) – permissible for exotic Asian currencies (e.g., CNY, TWD, KRW) used in syrup sourcing, with USD settlement through correspondent bank
Cross-Currency Swap (fixed-variable) – available for GIP/GBP to USD/EUR for cancellation of balance-sheet currency mismatch
Currency Option (call/put) – permitted for covered underwriting of franchise fee collections or inventory purchases
FX Swap (single-day roll) – used for liquidity closure between operational and capital accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Annual Return and Annual Government Fee (Companies Act 1981, s.120; e-filed by the licensed resident agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of incorporation; no registry extension is available. Fee bracket US$1,545 applies to authorised capital up to US$500,000 under the current Bermuda Registry schedule.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of BMD 50 per day subject to a BMD 1,000 cap; a further 90-day default triggers a Registrar strike-off notice and administrative dissolution under s.257, loss of exempted-company status and Bermuda tax-exemption certificate; directors incur personal daily fines of BMD 25.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation Return (Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2017)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Beneficial Ownership Database, Registrar of Companies, Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation; a BO Update Return must be filed within 30 days of any franchise-equity transfer or change in registrable beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Strict-liability offence: corporate and officer fines up to BMD 5,000 plus BMD 500 per day for continuing default; persistent non-compliance requires the licensed agent to terminate the relationship, after which the Registrar may cancel the exempted status and strike off the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Declaration and Annual Substance Report (Economic Substance (Substance Requirements) Act 2020) for relevant activities: Intellectual Property, Headquarters and Distribution-and-Service Centre
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Economic Substance Registry, Registrar of Companies, Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year end, aligned with the Bermuda group accounting period ending 31 December; the declaration is submitted in the same e-portal cycle as the annual return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil penalty up to BMD 10,000 plus BMD 500 per day for failure to file or for filing an inaccurate declaration; confirmed material non-compliance is reported to the OECD/Gibraltar competent authorities and may lead to withdrawal of the tax-exemption certificate and enforced revocation of the exempted licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Overseas Company Annual Return and Confirmation Statement (Companies Act 2014, Part 25) for the Gibraltar branch maintained as the Pan-European franchise and EMI-banking hub
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies, Companies House, Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 21 days after each anniversary of the overseas-company registration in Gibraltar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of GIP 50 to GIP 500 plus a continuing daily default fine; prolonged default causes removal of the Gibraltar overseas registration, loss of standing to enforce franchise agreements in Gibraltar, frozen EMI banking relations, and summary fines against directors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Bermuda exempted company must appoint a Bermuda-licensed auditor unless the Registrar grants an audit dispensation under Companies Act 1981 s.88A. The small-company dispensation requires: (i) fewer than 50 shareholders; (ii) no listed or publicly offered securities; (iii) unanimous shareholder consent; and (iv) balance-sheet total below BMD 1.0 million and annual revenue below BMD 2.0 million. The boba-tea franchise-IP and syrups-supply entity will exceed the revenue and asset de minimis thresholds, holds registrable trademarks generating royalties, and requires audited accounts for UK-group consolidation; therefore a full independent statutory audit is compulsory and the signed audited financial statements must be maintained at the registered office and produced to the Registrar or the Economic Substance Authority upon formal request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB is the governing framework; Bermuda does not prescribe a domestic statutory GAAP. The Gibraltar branch statutory accounting follows IFRS as applied in Gibraltar, and the ultimate United Kingdom parent consolidates under UK-adopted IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2017 and the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2018, the exempted company must maintain an accurate Register of Beneficial Owners at its registered office and file: (a) an initial BO Return within 30 days of incorporation; (b) an annual BO Confirmation within 60 days of the incorporation anniversary certifying the BO register is accurate; and (c) a BO Update Return within 30 days of any share transfer or change in registrable beneficial ownership. The operating protocol for the franchise holding is that the licensed corporate service provider circulates a Director's Certificate and the franchise-equity holding schedule 45 days before the anniversary; the confirmation is authorised by board resolution before submission. Share transfers, including franchise-equity dilutions and royalty-IP sub-licensing restructurings, are reported immediately and are never deferred to the annual confirmation cycle.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$ 3,200 – US$ 10,500 per annum for a Bermuda licensed corporate service provider covering registered office, resident secretary, statutory mail handling, e-portal annual-return preparation and BO/ESR filings; Gibraltar branch overseas-company compliance support is typically an additional US$ 1,400 – US$ 2,500 per annum.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$ 12,000 – US$ 35,000 per annum for a franchise-licensing and syrups-supply exempted company with intercompany royalty and inventory flows, assuming no complex transfer-pricing dispute and one Gibraltar branch; add US$ 5,000 – US$ 8,000 for mirrored Gibraltar branch audit procedures.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (with 10% standard Gibraltar headline rate applicable to non-exempt chargeable income)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Bermuda Exempted Company with no Gibraltar taxable local activity: effective nil rate on foreign-source franchise royalties and syrup supply; statutory tax exemptions under Bermuda law; Gibraltar exempt company certificates for qualifying foreign-source income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Form GST201 (Company Income Tax Return) and relevant Foreign Income Exemption declarations, filed through the Gibraltar Income Tax Office electronic filing portal (GIBTRO eFiling)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 12 months after the accounting period year-end, unless otherwise notified by the Commissioner; provisional payments may have quarterly or half-yearly interim obligations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company details: registered name, certificate of incorporation number, registered address (Gibraltar office), registered agent contact
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Gibraltar branch registration number and demonstrate registered agent; do not rely solely on Bermuda certificate unless dual registration is disclosed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax residence declaration and exempt status indication (e.g., 'Non-Resident Owned Exempt Company' or 'Exempt Company under Bermuda/Gibraltar arrangement')
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tick the exempt-company box; attach the Bermuda Exempted Company Certificate of Incorporation plus Gibraltar tax residence certificate where applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income: worldwide franchise royalties, syrup sales, franchise licensee fee income, bank interest, other operating revenues
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Break out income into Gibraltar-source (if local activity occurs) vs foreign-source; only foreign-source income qualifies for statutory exemption under the exempt regime

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: direct franchise brand cost, syrup procurement, marketing, legal and accounting, Gibraltar registered agent fees, staff/office costs (if any)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apportion deductions against chargeable income; do not deduct intercompany charges that fail arm's length or substance documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit calculation; reliefs under Double Taxation Arrangements (DTA) or unilateral relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty relief via the Gibraltar DTA protocol; include Form DT-1 submission and foreign tax credit evidence; maintain Bermuda tax residence proof for treaty certification

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Self-assessment declaration: confirm return is complete and accurate, sign/authorise registered agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be signed by a Gibraltar resident director or registered agent; signature constitutes legal declaration binding the foreign beneficial owner to the content

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: initial default penalty of GIP 100, escalating daily penalty up to GIP 10,000 maximum, plus Commissioner-issued assessment based on estimated income; interest accrues at 2% per month on unpaid tax; false declaration penalties up to GIP 1,000,000 and 12-month imprisonment

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Gibraltar does not impose withholding tax on dividends; Bermuda also has no dividend withholding tax)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No comprehensive DTA regime between Gibraltar and Bermuda, but Gibraltar's exempt/commercial and EU-legacy frameworks allow nil dividends to non-residents. Where a UK or other treaty partner claims beneficial ownership, the franchise holding must submit Form WT-DTA, certify beneficial ownership of the royalty/income stream, attach tax residence certificates, and apply through the Gibraltar Income Tax Office for reduced or nil treaty withholding before remittance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Gibraltar withholding on non-resident royalties and interest is generally 0% (none under domestic law); Bermuda imposes no withholding tax on IP royalties or debt interest; treaty rates range from 0% to 10% where a DTA applies (e.g., UK/Gibraltar arrangements); however, UK royalty source rules may assert UK withholding if the payer is UK-resident and economic substance is weak

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: GIP 5,000,000 annual related-party gross turnover, or GIP 1,000,000 for a single controlled transaction, triggers Local File maintenance; Master File required where group turnover exceeds GIP 25,000,000; Bermuda Economic Substance Regulations require records for all 'relevant activities' regardless of threshold
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Bermuda Exempted Company is subject to Bermuda Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) and must file an annual Economic Substance Declaration; franchise licensing and distribution activities are 'relevant activities'; annual board meetings, physical presence, and core income-generating activity in Bermuda required unless a tax-resident non-Bermuda exemption is separately certified; Gibraltar also imposes economic substance through EU-inspired rules, requiring sufficient local substance for pass-through income treatment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to declare franchise royalties or syrup procurement income; deliberately misrepresenting foreign-source status of income earned through a Gibraltar nexus; forging Bermuda exemption documents to evade Gibraltar tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to GIP 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years under Gibraltar Income Tax Act; daily principal sum equal to double the tax evaded; loss of exempt status; assessment at 10% standard rate with back interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners can be personally assessed for the tax, penalties, and costs; travel bans may be imposed by the Gibraltar Court; confiscation orders under Proceeds of Crime Act; prison time up to 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Bermuda Exempted Company with zero local employees, no board meetings in Bermuda, no controlled activity, and only a Gibraltar mailbox, while licensing global boba tea franchise IP and deriving income without substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Bermuda Economic Substance Regulations: penalty of BMD 50,000–BMD 350,000, plus BMD 10,000 per day for continued breach; Gibraltar equivalent failure may trigger strike-off and deregistration; assessments are made on income (10% on rev'd chargeable income) plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors have exposure to disqualification, travel bans, and civil restitution; failure to file economic substance declaration triggers personal criminal liability in Bermuda; director travel bans are judicially available in Gibraltar for economic substance non-compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering (Royalty Wire & Syrup Trade)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Franchise royalty wires routed through Gibraltar without proper AML/KYC controls; cash or wire payments for boba syrup concentrate from master franchisees in high-risk jurisdictions linked to sanctioned clients or unexplained wealth; failure to file suspicious activity reports (SAR)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Gibraltar Proceeds of Crime Act: fines up to GIP 500,000 or 10% of annual turnover; asset freezing orders; AML registration suspension; possible revocation of Gibraltar commercial licence; Bermuda counterpart sanctions apply under Proceeds of Crime Act 1997 (Bermuda)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors/officers personally liable for facilitating money laundering: imprisonment up to 14 years; unlimited financial penalties; confiscation of personal and corporate assets; travel bans as condition of bail or court order

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring syrup sales and franchise royalties through Bermuda subsidiary with no arm's length compensation, under-documentation of royalty pricing, or creating a UK/Gibraltar permanent establishment by having sales staff or a UK franchisee office taking orders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment to arm's length; penalty 20% of the revised profit adjustment; interest at 2% monthly; possible additional assessment of Gibraltar-source profit at 10%; UK-HMRC recharacterisation of PE could generate substantial UK corporate tax + surcharges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed incorrect TP documentation can be liable for civil penalties up to GIP 100,000; if dishonesty proved, personal criminal liability; UK director disqualification and travel bans may apply if the PE issue is litigated

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Maintain DTA / Beneficial Ownership Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Gibraltar/Bermuda jurisdiction to claim treaty benefits but failing to meet beneficial ownership requirements; excessive royalty payments to Irish/Netherlands/Bermuda holding vehicles without economic ownership; unreported beneficial owner changes on Gibraltar beneficial ownership register
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DTA relief denied; assessed at 10% full rate plus back taxes and interest; administrative penalties of GIP 500,000; potential exposure to EU ATAD/DAC6 reporting and cross-border arrangement penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability for unpaid taxes caused by failure to register beneficial owners; travel restrictions from Gibraltar; personal fines under Gibraltar Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations up to GIP 500,000; disqualification orders
